correspondences.description: The checked-in measurement report's 'outside the window' count was raised from 130 to 132 to match the current audit corpus, but that count is re-derived at test time from every diagnose audit under the live .forge/audits corpus, so the two audits written today (diagnose-issue-2947 and diagnose-issue-2948, both stamped 2026-09-07T08:39:52Z, after the report's fixed 'until' bound) are what moved it, and the next diagnose run moves it again and re-fails the baseline gate.

A diagnose audit whose started_at field is empty or not an ISO-8601 timestamp is now parsed unguarded during cohort selection, so it raises an uncaught ValueError that aborts the whole measurement run, whereas the same record was previously classified as out-of-window and the report still rendered.

The landed_commit fact for each in-window issue is re-derived from a live git log over the integration refs and is compared as a drift field, so when a commit whose subject matches the title of an issue currently recorded as having landed nothing (#2910 and #2926 in the checked-in record) reaches main, the run stops with an adjudication-does-not-match-the-corpus error and the byte-for-byte report check fails again.

finding_registry.description: The checked-in measurement report's 'outside the window' count was raised from 130 to 132 to match the current audit corpus, but that count is re-derived at test time from every diagnose audit under the live .forge/audits corpus, so the two audits written today (diagnose-issue-2947 and diagnose-issue-2948, both stamped 2026-09-07T08:39:52Z, after the report's fixed 'until' bound) are what moved it, and the next diagnose run moves it again and re-fails the baseline gate.

A diagnose audit whose started_at field is empty or not an ISO-8601 timestamp is now parsed unguarded during cohort selection, so it raises an uncaught ValueError that aborts the whole measurement run, whereas the same record was previously classified as out-of-window and the report still rendered.

The landed_commit fact for each in-window issue is re-derived from a live git log over the integration refs and is compared as a drift field, so when a commit whose subject matches the title of an issue currently recorded as having landed nothing (#2910 and #2926 in the checked-in record) reaches main, the run stops with an adjudication-does-not-match-the-corpus error and the byte-for-byte report check fails again.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
